question: Women with PCOS have an increased lifetime risk of endometrial carcinoma, primarily because chronic anovulation leads to prolonged unopposed oestrogen stimulation of the endometrium.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. In PCOS, chronic anovulation means there is no luteal-phase progesterone to oppose oestrogen. Prolonged oestrogen stimulation of the endometrium leads to hyperplasia and a significantly increased risk of endometrial carcinoma — one important reason to ensure regular menstrual withdrawal in anovulatory women.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Without progesterone withdrawal from regular ovulatory cycles, the endometrium is exposed to sustained oestrogenic stimulation, leading to endometrial hyperplasia and a 3-fold increased risk of endometrial carcinoma. Regular endometrial shedding (via COC or progestogen) is therefore a preventive intervention.
